_doc: Medium batch m05 themed pass (Opus): 9 crabs. Every crab has its own signature motif (module claude/pf-anim/motifs/medium_m05.js, 29 motifs); crab-clamp (one big claw) and surf-foam are shared secondaries tinted by each palette. Small motifs reused where truly the same: magpie-trinket (the robber crab steals shiny things), shell-click (three shells), mud-flop (mire), ink-cloud (silt). All 8 pieces per creature carry a hand note.

shore-crab.notes: Common olive-green shore crab of the tideline: shuffles sideways, digs into wet sand until only the eyestalks show, raises and clacks its claws as a warning.

p.b0: Sideways Snip: olive crabs sidle off the edge one after another, claws snipping, leg ticks left in the sand

b1.n: Shoreline Spray: small blue wavelets curl off the edge and break into white spray

b2.n: Sand Shell Shield: crabs sink into the sand along the edge, only the eyestalks up, sand kicked over them

p.b3: Sidestep Shuffle: crabs hang sideways at spots tied by sand lines, shuffling left and right

u0.n: Pinch: one olive claw runs the length of the edge and snaps shut at the end

u1.n: Shell Up: crabs dig into the wet sand and hold, eyestalks ducking, bubbles rising

u2.n: Sidestep: the crabs scuttle out sideways and back, sand dust behind

u3.n: Clack Warn: raised claw pairs pop up at spots and clack shut, white click marks

ghost-crab.notes: Pale sand-coloured night beach crab with huge black eyes on stalks: runs so fast it seems to vanish, lives in burrows and flicks rolled sand balls.

b0.n: Burrow Grab Snap: claws snap up out of burrow mouths and drop back in

b1.n: Sand Burst Flick: rolled sand balls are flicked off the edge in little arcs, grains trailing

b2.n: Sand Camouflage: pale crabs line the edge and flicker into the sand haze

b3.n: Vanishing Dash: a pale crab blinks from spot to spot, gone before you look

p.u0: Ghost Dash: ghost crabs slam out and back so fast they flicker; the chain is an afterimage dash

u1.n: Sand Throw: sand balls pop up at spots in quick flicks, dust puffing

u2.n: Pale Hide: burrow mouths push out along the edge, only black eyestalks showing

u3.n: Bolt Pinch: pale claws bolt off the edge and snap, a streak behind

land-crab-march.notes: Broad scarlet land crabs on their great migration from the rainforest to the sea: a long red line over roads and roots, shaking eggs into the surf.

b0.n: Red Pincer Snap: scarlet claws lunge off the edge and snap

b1.n: Sea-Bound Surge: surf crests full of dark egg specks surge off the edge

b2.n: Red Shell Wall: red backs push out edge to edge like a raised wall

p.b3: Speed-Bump Shove: red crabs hang at spots tied in a line, a migration that will not move
p.u0: Carapace Wall: broad red backs line the edge and hold, a shine sliding across

u1.n: Burrow Cover: fallen leaves lie over the burrows along the edge; one lifts and a red claw peeks out

u2.n: Sidestep Clamp: the column sidesteps down the edge in one file, claws clamping

u3.n: March Trample: the red line slams out and drops back in a dust cloud; the column streams on

palm-thief-crab.notes: Huge blue-purple robber crab of the island palms with oversized claws and orange legs: climbs palms, cracks coconuts and sneaks off with anything shiny.

b0.n: Coconut-Cracking Pinch: coconuts lunge off the edge and crack open, white flesh showing

b1.n: Dusk Palm Splash: palm fronds slap out into the water and back, bubbles rising

b2.n: Palm-Shadow Shell: robber crabs crouch along the edge in palm shade, a dusk haze over them

p.b3: Thieving Tide Grab: big claws hang at spots tied together, creeping then snatching

u0.n: Palm Husk Wall: tan coir fibres line the edge and hold, tips curling

p.u1: Coconut Cover: palm fronds are pulled over the edge like a roof and held, swaying

u2.n: Fruit Throw: coconuts slam out and split; the chain lobs one in an arc to the next piece

u3.n: Sly Fetch: stolen rings and coins rise off the edge, glinting, as the robber makes off

hermit-crab-hoarder.notes: A hermit crab that cannot stop collecting: its shell is piled with bottle caps, sea glass and coins, it staggers under the load and keeps spare shells.

b0.n: Borrowed Pincer: an orange hermit claw lunges out of the shell and snaps

b1.n: Shell Swap Splash: empty shells are kicked off the edge in a splash of bubbles

b2.n: Triple Shell: three different shells line up along the edge, clicking

b3.n: Shell Hunt Dive: the hermit pops in and out of shells at spot after spot, bubbles rising

u0.n: Borrowed Shell: loaded shells line the edge and hold, the junk wobbling on top

u1.n: Hoard Toss: a bottle cap, a button, sea glass and a coin are tossed off the edge, turning over

p.u2: Shell Swap: empty shells rise off the edge as the soft hermit pops from one into the next

u3.n: Spare Address: a row of spare shells parked along the edge, a sheen on each doorway

coconut-hermit.notes: An orange hermit crab living in half a coconut shell: rolls and thumps about on island sand and forest floor, sips coconut milk to heal (drain).

b0.n: Coconut Clamp: orange claws lunge out from under the coconut and snap, husk flakes falling

b1.n: Milk Drench: white coconut-milk drops fall off the edge

b2.n: Mended Coconut Shell: coconut halves along the edge close up and hold, a stitch of light on the seam

b3.n: Shell Slide: a coconut house slides down the length of the edge on a wet trail

p.u0: Husk Thump: the coconut house thumps down the edge in one line; the chain is the house rolling on

u1.n: Milk Sip: milk drops rise off the edge as the crab sips, little bubbles

u2.n: Husk Cover: tan coir fibres bristle out of the edge like spikes

u3.n: Coconut Mend: split coconuts rise and close back together, a light stitch on the seam

rock-crab-pincher.notes: Flat dark-red wedge-shaped rock crab of island reefs: wary, it lives in rock cracks and pools and pinches from a crevice.

b0.n: Crack-Wedge Pincer: dark-red claws lunge out of the rock and snap

p.b1: Crevice Jab: flat crabs shoot claws first out of rock cracks and off the edge

b2.n: Flat Red Carapace: wedge crabs sit half out of their cracks along the edge and hold

b3.n: Rock Crack Lure: little rock pools hang at spots tied together, a bright glint as bait

u0.n: Clamp Snap: quick claws snap off the edge with click marks; the chain zigzags on

u1.n: Pool Hide: rock pools scatter out and back, two claw tips peeking from the water

u2.n: Tide Pool Cover: rock pools line the edge and hold, weed swaying, bubbles rising

p.u3: Wedged Claw: a wedge crab squeezes down the edge in one line; the chain is a crack it runs along

mud-crab-brawler.notes: Dark mud-brown brawler of wetland and coast with heavy blunt crusher claws held up like boxing mitts; lobs mud and regrows a lost claw.

p.b0: Mire Pincer Crush: heavy mitt claws lunge off the edge jabbing in turn

b1.n: Mud Bomb Splash: fat dripping mud balls are lobbed off the edge and splat

b2.n: Regrowing Carapace: green claw buds along the edge swell to full claws and hold

b3.n: Sinking Mire Pull: mud splats hang at spots tied together, flopping as they suck down

p.u0: Mud Mend: green buds rise off the edge and grow into new claws

u1.n: Mud Crack: the crusher mitts slam out and drop back, mud clods flying

u2.n: Silt Cloak: brown silt puffs bloom out and settle back

u3.n: Mire Pinch: the mitts jab down the length of the edge in one line, mud dust behind

tide-crab-squire.notes: Small sea-blue crab squire with a patched shell and proudly polished claws: carries a limpet as a buckler and charges stubbornly into the tide.

b0.n: Apprentice Pincer Snap: polished claws lunge off the edge and snap, white sheen flecks

b1.n: Tidewave Splash: sea-blue wavelets curl off the edge and break into white spray

b2.n: Young Shell Plate: limpet bucklers push out along the edge like a raised guard

b3.n: Stubborn Tide Charge: a squire charges down the edge into the tide, bubbles rising

u0.n: Squire Nip: little squires dart off the edge, the gleam swapping claw to claw

u1.n: Sidle Pinch: squires sidle out and back pinching, the patch on each shell showing

u2.n: Shell Patch: limpet bucklers line the edge and hold, a glint at each peak

u3.n: Stubborn Pinch: a polished claw slams out and back, click marks at the snap
